subject: Repeated measures, serial mediators, specific hypothesis test

messages.author: a20b653f7e0884b9
messages.subject: Repeated measures, serial mediators, specific hypothesis test
parts:
Hi all, 

I am coming to you with a question that me and my co-authors have been stumped for the last several weeks.

We ran a study with a factorial repeated measures design where we had a 2 (first info: Pos vs. Neg) x 2 (second info: Pos vs. Neg) design resulting in four factors (PP, PN, NP, NN) that all subjects went through. We also measured four mediators of interest. We expected an averaging effect, i.e. that people would evaluate the PP condition most positively, the PN and NP condition somewhere in the middle, and the NN as least positively. This is what we obtained. 

We now want to incorporate the averaging hypothesis into our mediation and test it effectively and we want to insert our four mediators where we want to test single and possible serial mediation. The question is therefore twofold: 

1) what  would be the correct way to incorporate our hypothesis into the mediation model? For instance, should there be several mediation tests, e.g. comparing PP to NN, PP to PN and NP etc. or is there some other way? How does lavaan treat repeated measure designs?
 
2) what would be the best way to incorporate four mediators to test both single and serial mediations (e.g. X-M1-M2-Y) given the specifics of our design (I'm a bit of a lavaan newbie but the question is mainly to verify if there are any special considerations for repeated measures designs) ? 

Any advice or help you could spare on this would be much appreciated as we have been at a dead end for quite some time regarding this issue. 

Thanks, 
Emir
